hero.heroPara: International students planning to study in France can choose between French-taught and English-taught programs, requiring specific French language diplomas (DELF, DALF, TCF, TEF) or accepted English tests (IELTS, TOEFL) for Campus France and university admission.

overview: France is a premier European destination for Indian students seeking top-notch education, globally recognized credentials, and worldwide employment opportunities across management, engineering, fashion, and sciences.
Your chosen university, program language of instruction, academic background, and professional goals determine the specific examinations you must take.
While programs taught in French require certified French language proficiency (DELF, DALF, TCF, or TEF), thousands of programs taught entirely in English accept IELTS or TOEFL.

faqs.q: What test is needed to study in France?
faqs.a: It depends on the language of instruction. French-taught degrees generally require DELF B2 or DALF C1, or an equivalent TCF/TEF score. Programs taught in English require IELTS (6.0–7.0) or TOEFL iBT (80–100).

faqs.q: Is taking the IELTS required in France?
faqs.a: No, IELTS is not mandatory for all programs. If you enroll in a French-taught course, French diplomas (DELF/DALF) are required. For English-taught programs, universities accept TOEFL or PTE as alternatives.

faqs.q: Is it possible for me to take an online French language test from India?
faqs.a: Certain TCF sessions and partnerships may offer digital/computer-based options at authorized centers. However, official DELF and DALF diplomas must be taken in-person during official examination sessions at authorized Alliance Française centers.

faqs.q: What is the validity period for French language exam results?
faqs.a: DELF and DALF diplomas have perpetual (lifetime) validity. TCF test score reports are valid for two years. TEF validity is also generally two years depending on the specific test variant.
